To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Enterococcus species isolates from poultry sources are resistant to multiple antibiotics and are positive for vancomycin genes.

Enterococcus spp., especially E. faecali, E. duran, E. hira and E. casseliflavis isolated from poultry in Malaysia were multi-resistance, harboured vanA and van C2/C3 genes, and were genetically diverse.

(1) the vanA and the vanC2/C genes are the predominant van genes detected in Enterococcus spp., (2) the vanA gene is present only in Enterococcus isolatess that are resistant to vancomycin, (3) the Enterococcus species are highly polymorphic and genetically distinct, and (4) the vanA genes were found to be associated with plasmids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence and characterization of Enterococcus species and the detection of vancomycin resistance genes in Enterococci isolates from poultry sources in the country.

the occurrence and diversity of vancomycin resistant enterococci (VRE) isolated from food animals in Malaysia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Enterococcus spp., especially E. faecali, E. faecim and E. casseliflavis, are the potential reservoir for VRE and should not be ignored.
Enterococcus spp., especially E. faecum and E. faescalis, are the most important pathogens in poultry and the vanA gene is the most important gene in poultry Enterococci in Malaysia.

Enterococcus spp., particularly E. faecaliis and E. faeimun, are the predominant species of the Enterococci in poultry sources in Malaysia, which are also multi-resistant to the antibiotics used in the study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) are widely distributed among poultry sources.
Enterococcus spp are resistant to a variety of antibiotics and that plasmids are the main vehicle of resistance.

Enterococcus spp., especially E. faecialis and E. durans isolates from poultry sources are potential sources of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in poultry production and in the food chain, as well as in the environment and human infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Enterococcus species are highly resistant to antibiotics and that they can be a source of VRE.
Enterococcus spp are a reservoir for vanA and vanB resistance genes in poultry and the potential to spread these resistance genes to other bacteria.
the poultry industry is a source of Enterococcus spp., which can be a reservoir of VRE.
